item.title: Chesapeake high-speed internet project will expand connectivity
item.description: Chesapeake officials say the city is the first to complete its portion of a regional broadband ring connecting south Hampton Roads cities as it works to complete its own fiber optic network that will expand internet options across Chesapeake.

item.title: Member of Trump’s Religious Liberty Commission ousted in dispute over antisemitism
item.description: The ousted member, Carrie Prejean Boller, had defended commentator Candace Owens.

item.title: UVA running back J’Mari Taylor invited to NFL combine
item.description: In other region/state news, Virginia Tech has revised its season-opening baseball series schedule against William & Mary in Blacksburg. The teams will now play a 3 p.m. game Friday and a 1 p.m. doubleheader Saturday with inclement weather in the forecast for Sunday.

item.title: Photos: ODU gives up 17 point lead in loss to Marshall
item.description: The Old Dominion Monarchs lost to the Marshall Thundering Herd 81-79 after giving up a 17 point lead at Chartway Arena in Norfolk, Va., on Feb. 11, 2026.

item.title: ODU women fall to Coastal Carolina, CNU and VWU men win
item.description: Simaru Fields led ODU with 14 points and En'Dya Buford added 12, but went 2 of 14 from the field.

item.title: Virginia Tech gets résumé-building victory on the road at No. 20 Clemson
item.description: Jailen Bedford scored 23 points, Ben Hammond had 17 of his 19 points in the second half, and Virginia Tech kept the Tigers out of a first-place Atlantic Coast Conference tie with No. 4 Duke.

item.title: High school scoreboard: Manor stuns No. 4 Lake Taylor in boys basketball upset
item.description: No. 1 Princess Anne earned their 21st girls basketball victory of the season by defeating Landstown 85-33.

item.title: ODU men squander 17-point lead in loss to Marshall
item.description: Marshall shot 62% from the field and made 7 of 11 3-pointers in the second half, scoring eight of the final 10 points of the game.

item.title: Landstown High grad Donald Hand Jr. leaves Boston College loss with injury
item.description: He got up with assistance and was walking in the locker room afterward, but his immediate future is unclear.
